example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, the October 2026 close, Day 1 on Monday 2 November. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

chosen.close-template.xlsx: the name of the user's own close template with the task owners
chosen.september-close-pack.xlsx: the name of the user's own September close pack

messages.text: Can you set up our October close and keep track of it?
Yes. Before I read anything, I need some answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload the data?
What is your close calendar, or your target close date?
Is this a soft close or a hard close?
Which reporting framework do you use?
Who owns each task? Roles are fine.
Do you have a close template, and last month's close?
Do you report on a cash or an accrual basis?

messages.text: Use MosoFin. October 2026, in seven business days from Monday 2 November. Hard close, US GAAP, accrual. The owners are in our template. Materiality is $5,000. The September close pack is attached too.

messages.label: Checked the workspace and the company file
rows: One company file, confirmed by name
messages.summary: The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

messages.text: Here is my plan. I plan the **October 2026** close for **Northbrook Trading**, one entity in one currency, so there is no consolidation day. Day 1 is **Monday 2 November** and Day 7 is **Tuesday 10 November**. It is a hard close, US GAAP, accrual, with materiality of **$5,000**. Shall I start?

messages.label: Read the books in one batch
messages.summary: 8 reads in one batch. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: My standard list has 48 tasks on Days 1 to 7. I fitted it to your books. Each change has its evidence:

card.title: Your October list
head: Evidence
Tasks
Change
rows: No inventory account in the chart
Remove inventory cutoff, cycle count and write-downs
Professional services, with accounts behind them
Add WIP unbilled and project profitability

messages.after: With the 5 pre-close tasks, you have 46. Each task has an owner from your template, a due day and its dependencies. You use the accrual basis, so the accruals stay on Day 1 and Day 3.

messages.text: It is Wednesday, Day 3. Where are we?

messages.label: Read the October entries
messages.summary: 1 read, and your template. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: Three close entries are in the books. I check each task against the books, not only against the template:
messages.after: Deferred revenue release is due today, and no entry exists yet. It is still open.

messages.text: One line does not agree. Your template marks the **payroll cutoff accrual** as Complete, but no entry is posted. Please ask its owner before the books lock.

card.title: What the books cannot show
head: Item
Status
Who moves it
rows: The owner reconciles against the bank statement

messages.after: I show Crestline's statement in a separate group, because nobody inside the books can move it.

messages.text: Day 7 now. Can you run the tie-out?

messages.label: Read the tie-out evidence
messages.summary: 3 reads, and your close pack. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: Every balance sheet account must open October where September closed. Five of seven agree. Two do not:

card.title: September, as reported and in the books now
head: Account
Difference
As reported
In the books now

messages.after: The sum is 0, so someone moved **$500** from AP to accrued liabilities. The entry is dated 30 September, and someone posted it on Tuesday 20 October, after you reported September. It may be proper. Someone must know about it before October's statements go out.

messages.text: One task slips every month. **Deferred revenue release** is due on Day 3. In August and in September, someone entered it on Day 6. That is 3 days late, two months in a row. I measured it from the entry-created times.
messages.after: I never lock the books, post an entry or mark a task complete. Your workpaper has nine sheets. Do you want it as an Excel file? And do you want me to save your settings for November?

messages.text: Done. The Excel file has the nine sheets. I saved the task list, the owners by role, the dependencies, the calendar and the materiality threshold. I never save statuses or balances. Next month, I read every status again.
